method: Reviewed each displayed sentence and all four choices item by item, independently determining whether the reduced clause had active or passive voice from the relationship between the participle and the main-clause subject before comparing with the stored key/explanation. Checked unique-answer validity, sentence naturalness, target-skill fit, distractor plausibility, subject-control consistency, tense/voice compatibility, and explanation consistency. The persisted candidate format co-locates keys with stems, so strict technical answer-blinding cannot be guaranteed in this connector-only path; no item was approved without individual review.
notes: All 25 items require a passive reduced participle clause: in every sentence, the main-clause subject receives the action expressed by the opening participle phrase, so the past participle is uniquely defensible among the four choices. No dangling-subject conflict, competing infinitive/base-form/-ing reading, or explanation inconsistency was found. Full cross-bank semantic near-duplicate clearance remains outstanding.
